# Layers

Where gragas's Go code lives, and what each package may import. The folders follow the Go program template of go.layout.1, with its names: the bounded contexts under `internal/core/`, the operations every command calls in `internal/core/api`, one port package with its fake, the adapters under `internal/host/<tool>/`, config, the command tree under `internal/cli/<group>/`, leaves, and `cmd/gragas`, which wires everything by hand. Two more tables follow the layers: the contexts, which never import one another, and the explorer's modules, which have the same contract in TypeScript.

Every package may also import its own package, and its tests the stand-ins. A test obeys its package's row (arch.layers.10). A package marked planned does not exist yet: it joins its row in the pull request that creates it, and the rows already hold it to this table.

## Where the template puts each layer

- **entry.** `cmd/<name>`: wires and registers, nothing else. A breach says: go.layout.1, arch.ports.13: cmd/gragas wires the adapters into the ports, checks the table of endings before anything runs and runs the command tree; it hands the plugin host the engine's codec (core/wire) and judgement of a manifest (core/plugins), since an adapter never imports the core (arch.layers.7); its test binds the Steps port main fills with a plugin scope, the types-only leaf model/plugin.
- **entry-subset.** `cmd/gragas-subset`: built by the gate in every run and shipped nowhere. A breach says: arch.layers.13: the explorer stays separable, so the subset entry never imports host/assets.
- **cli.** `cli/<group>`: the root and one group per context; it draws only through the Terminal port, so there is no `cli/ui`. A breach says: arch.ports.2: a command reaches the core through its operations and the world through the ports main fills; no adapter, no context.
- **cli-cmd.** `cli/cmd/<command>`: one package per command family; it draws only through the session the root hands it. A breach says: arch.ports.2: a command package reaches the core through its operations and the run through the kit's session; no adapter, no context, no root and no other command.
- **cli-planned.** `cli/planned/<name>.yaml`: a row of the table of spec 15.1 that has no code yet, so it is data, absent from the command tree. A breach says: arch.layers.1: the planned list is data and a loader over the kit; it imports the kit, the model and the leaves, no library, no root. Its standard packages, and no other: `embed`, `errors`, `fmt`, `io/fs`, `slices`, `strings`.
- **cli-kit.** `cli/kit`: what every command shares, free of cobra, so a command package and the root both build on it. A breach says: arch.layers.1: the kit is a leaf of the command tree; it imports the model and the standard packages it lists, no library, no adapter, no root. Its standard packages, and no other: `context`, `errors`, `fmt`, `slices`, `strconv`, `strings`.
- **cli-run.** `cli/run`: the form every plan command ends in, free of cobra (arch.ports.6); the root says whether a command takes --apply and was given it. A breach says: arch.ports.2: the seam reaches the core through its operations; no adapter, no root, no cobra.
- **legacy-cli.** Temporary. The old commands are one package until the contexts' commands replace them at the M6 cut-over; only cli/root imports it (M0a-20). A breach says: arch.ports.2: a command reaches the core through its operations and the world through the ports the root hands it; no adapter, no context. Temporary: this row is gone by M6.
- **coreapi.** `core/api`: the operations every client calls and their result types; the package is named coreapi, as arch.structure.7's check refuses api. A breach says: arch.layers.1: the operations import the contexts, the port and the leaves, nothing above them; internal/model/contract is the bundle a parent's rules are read from, turned into the context's argument here; internal/model/plugin is the plugin contract's types, which the import's bridge over the adapter reader gives link as a plugin's entries until Ports.Plugins is wired; internal/core/plugins is the plan rounds those entries are asked through, which its tests compose over the stand-in; internal/pluginbundle is the one judge of a bundle as read, which plugin list asks for the tool a row shows. Its standard packages, and no other: `bytes`, `context`, `encoding/base64`, `encoding/json`, `errors`, `fmt`, `io`, `io/fs`, `maps`, `path`, `slices`, `strconv`, `strings`, `time`, `unicode/utf8`.
- **core.** `core`: the decisions. The template keeps its core in one package, internal/core; gragas has nine contexts, and arch.ports.8 asks that no context import another, through an independence contract listing them, so each is its own package under internal/core/ (go.layout.1 names internal/core/ the domain) and the contexts: table is that contract. A context that reads another declares the interface on its own side; internal/core/api, the operations, is where they meet. A breach says: arch.ports.1, arch.ports.8: a context imports the port and the leaves, never an adapter, the operating system, the network or another context; go/parser, go/token and go/build/constraint read a Go file's text up to its package clause, as audit's os-files reads it (arch.ports.24); internal/model/plugin is the plugin contract's generated types, which link reads a plugin's entries in. Its standard packages, and no other: `bufio`, `bytes`, `cmp`, `context`, `encoding/hex`, `errors`, `fmt`, `go/build/constraint`, `go/parser`, `go/scanner`, `go/token`, `io`, `io/fs`, `path`, `regexp`, `slices`, `strconv`, `strings`, `time`, `unicode`.
- **contract.** `contract`: a context like the core row's, in its own row for one leaf more: internal/model/contract, the generated types, which no other context reads yet. Each type's generated ToCanon and FromCanon turn a model value into canon's Value tree and a document that passed canon.Decode and its schema back into its model type, so the context reads and writes JSON through canon alone and imports no encoding/json. A breach says: arch.ports.1, arch.ports.8: a context imports the port and the leaves, never an adapter, the operating system, the network or another context; internal/model/contract is the one leaf more, and it reads and writes JSON through canon. Its standard packages, and no other: `bufio`, `bytes`, `cmp`, `context`, `encoding/hex`, `errors`, `fmt`, `io`, `io/fs`, `path`, `regexp`, `slices`, `strings`, `time`, `unicode`.
- **legacy-core.** Temporary. rulebook and generate are domains of the engine before its contexts, each its own package under internal/core/ with no import of the other: a domain that reads another declares the interface on its own side (generate's Book). The contexts of the core row replace them. A breach says: arch.ports.1, arch.ports.8: a domain imports the port and the leaves; another domain only through an interface it declares. ## The contexts

arch.ports.8: no context imports another; what one needs from another arrives as an argument, and the contexts meet only in internal/core/api The contexts are `internal/core/link`, `internal/core/proof`, `internal/core/format`, `internal/core/lifecycle`, `internal/core/release`, `internal/core/publish`, `internal/core/project`, `internal/core/audit`, `internal/core/agents`, `internal/core/contract`, `internal/core/plugins`. Each has a rule of its own in `.golangci.yml` that refuses the other eight, beside what its layer's row leaves out.

## What only an edge or an adapter imports

arch.ports.1: the core reaches the operating system, the network and other programs only through a port: `os`, `os/exec`, `net$`, `net/http`, `syscall`, `unsafe`, `plugin`. A trailing `$` matches the path exactly. A pure package refuses these calls too, in its non-test files; a test and the host layer call them with std: `github.com/birdtable/go-files/appdirs.Free`, `github.com/birdtable/go-files/appdirs.Here`, `github.com/birdtable/go-files/appdirs.Temp`, `github.com/birdtable/go-files/appdirs.TempOverflow`, `path/filepath.Abs`, `path/filepath.EvalSymlinks`, `path/filepath.Glob`, `path/filepath.Walk`, `path/filepath.WalkDir`.

## The ports

| Port | Subject | Adapter |
|---|---|---|
| `Tree` | a root's files, read-only: a rulebook's repository, a project, the engine's own state folder | `internal/host/fs` |
| `Writer` | one file replaced whole, or one line appended, inside a root | `internal/host/fs` |
| `Lock` | one writer per root at a time, and proof's scratch lock | `internal/host/fs` |
| `Journal` | the record of a run that writes: intent before effect, the plan, the copies, the close | `internal/host/fs` |
| `History` | a repository's own history, read-only | `internal/host/git` |
| `Remote` | releases from elsewhere, and the two writes release makes | `internal/host/git` |
| `Sandbox` | a prepared run at a named level | `internal/host/sandbox` |
| `Schema` | a document checked against a JSON Schema | `internal/host/jsonschema` |
| `Clock` | today, and the run time | `internal/host/clock` |
| `Assets` | the embedded files: the explorer app, the handbook, the schemas, the profiles, the fixture rulebook | `internal/host/assets` |
| `Terminal` | the person's terminal: width, colour depth, a question, a line out, a line in | `internal/host/term` |
| `Owned` | one file outside every root, read whole, that the settings name by an absolute path and only this account or root owns | `internal/host/fs` |
| `FileNames` | what a disk does with a file's name: its key where a disk folds names, or a refusal | `internal/host/fs` |
| `Trust` | the plugins a person approved to run on this machine, each by its bundle's digest, kept in the state folder and never in a clone | `internal/host/fs` |
| `Steps` | a plugin's steps of one read, each run or read under its manifest's grants alone, journalled before it starts | `internal/host/tool` |
| `Bundles` | the plugin bundles installed under a root as they lie on disk: the lock's list, and each bundle's files and digests as read | `internal/host/fs` |
| `Plugins` | the installed plugins of a root, each opened over its bundle and refused before any of its code runs, and each call one fresh instance of its module | `internal/host/plugin` |

`internal/port/testing` fills every port in memory. The port package's other interfaces are the values a port hands back: `Bundles`, `Plugin`, `Plugins`, `StepRunner`, `Trial`.

## The outside programs

Each outside program is started from one adapter package, by the absolute path its setting names, checked, with a fixed argv (arch.ports.6, cli.process.1). gosec's G204 sees a variable path there, and the ban of exec.Command and exec.CommandContext holds everywhere a test or a project's own row does not spare, so a generated block in `.golangci.yml` spares the non-test files of these adapters from both, and of no other package. A program joins this table in the pull request that builds its adapter.

| Program | Adapter |
|---|---|
| `git` | `internal/host/git` |
| `enforcer` | `internal/host/tool` |

## Platform words

No non-test file of a pure package starts a string with `/sys`, `/proc`, `/run`, `/opt`, `/etc`, `/var`, `/usr`, `/Library`, `/System`, `C:\` in any case, names `systemctl`, `systemd-run`, `journalctl`, `launchctl`, `apt-get`, `dpkg`, `brew`, `dnf`, `yum`, `pacman`, `powershell`, `diskutil`, `pmset`, or names a system folder below a home, `Library/LaunchAgents`, `Library/LaunchDaemons`, `Library/Application Support`, `Library/Preferences`, `.config/systemd`, `.local/share/systemd`, `AppData/`; no port and no fake names `linux`, `darwin`, `windows`, `macos`, `freebsd` (arch.ports.4, arch.ports.5, arch.ports.17). There is no exception list: the fix for a finding is a port.

## Source words

No Go string and no name in `internal/core`, `internal/cli` is a rule id (shape `\b[a-z][a-z0-9]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9-]*\.[0-9]+\b`), names `golangci-lint`, `eslint`, `tsc`, `ast-grep`, `depguard`, `ruff`, `mypy`, `prettier`, `biome`, `semgrep`, `gitleaks`, `govulncheck`, `staticcheck`, `gosec` or names the config formats `.golangci.yml`, `.eslintrc`, `eslint.config`, `pyproject.toml`, `ruff.toml`, `biome.json`, `.prettierrc`, `.gitleaks.toml`: rules and tools are data in adapters, and host/tool runs them (arch.ports.2). No package is named `util`, `utils`, `common`, `helpers`, `types`, `misc`, `api` (arch.structure.7), the files of layer `coreapi` stay under 300 lines, and init functions outside main number at most 0, a count that only falls.

## How the table is held

`task gen` runs `gragas-dev layers`, which writes this file, the block of depguard rows in `.golangci.yml` and `docs/explorer-boundaries.json` from `layers.yaml`; `task generated-files` runs it with `--check` and fails when any of them differs. `internal/layers_test.go` holds the tree to the same table with `go list`: every package in one row, every import of a non-test file and of a test on an edge its row allows, each library imported by its owner alone, the layout of go.layout.1, and the ports.
